item.content:encoded:
The Government of Japan is inviting applications from young South Africans interested in gaining international teaching and cultural exchange experience through the Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme 2027. The programme offers successful participants an opportunity to spend at least one year in Japan working as Assistant Language Teachers (ALTs) while contributing to internationalisation, foreign-language education, and people-to-people exchange at the local level.

Administered through a collaboration involving Japanese government ministries and agencies, the JET Programme is one of the world’s largest international exchange programmes. It brings university graduates from participating countries to Japan to work with local governments, schools, boards of education, and other organisations.

For South African graduates with an interest in education, language, Japanese culture, international relations, community engagement, and cross-cultural communication, the JET Programme provides an opportunity to live and work in Japan while developing professional and intercultural skills.

JET Programme 2027 Overview

The Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme was established to promote grassroots internationalisation in Japan. Participants work with local communities and educational institutions, helping strengthen understanding between Japan and other countries.

For the 2027 intake, the Embassy of Japan in South Africa is calling for applications from young South Africans who would like to spend at least one year in Japan as Assistant Language Teachers.

Key details

  • Programme: Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme
  • 2027 Position: Assistant Language Teacher (ALT)
  • Host country: Japan
  • Recruiting country: South Africa
  • Duration: Generally one year
  • Target applicants: Young South African university graduates
  • Work environment: Elementary, junior high and senior high schools, local boards of education and related institutions
  • Application method: Courier with a tracking number or hand delivery
  • Application deadline: 4:00 PM, 16 October 2026
  • Application location: Embassy of Japan, 259 Baines Street, Groenkloof, Pretoria, 0181
  • Selection notification: Successful and unsuccessful applicants will be contacted by email

What Is the JET Programme?

The JET Programme is an international exchange initiative administered through cooperation among several Japanese institutions, including the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), and the Council of Local Authorities for International Relations (CLAIR).

Its primary objective is to promote grassroots internationalisation at the local level.

Rather than focusing only on international exchange at the national or diplomatic level, the programme places participants directly within Japanese communities. Participants interact with students, teachers, local government employees and community members, allowing cultural exchange to take place through everyday professional and community activities.

The programme also seeks to create long-term international networks. Participants are expected to contribute positively to mutual understanding between Japan and their home countries while gaining a deeper understanding of Japanese society and culture.

JET Programme History and Global Reach

The JET Programme has developed considerably since its establishment in 1987.

According to the Embassy of Japan in South Africa, the programme began with participants from only four countries. Over the years, it has expanded to include participants from 54 countries, with 5,993 participants as of 2025.

Across the history of the programme, more than 80,000 people from 82 countries have participated.

This extensive international participation demonstrates the scale of the JET Programme and its emphasis on creating connections between Japan and communities around the world.

The programme has also developed a strong reputation both within Japan and internationally. Participants are regarded as representatives of their respective countries and are therefore expected to conduct themselves responsibly and contribute constructively to international understanding.

Assistant Language Teacher Position

The 2027 opportunity highlighted by the Embassy of Japan in South Africa is for applicants interested in serving as Assistant Language Teachers (ALTs).

ALTs are primarily placed in educational settings, including:

  • Local boards of education
  • Elementary schools
  • Junior high schools
  • Senior high schools

Participants work under the guidance of language-teacher consultants, Japanese teachers of foreign languages, school principals, boards of education, or other designated supervisors.

The precise working environment and responsibilities can vary depending on the Contracting Organisation to which an individual is assigned.

Duties and Responsibilities of an ALT

The role is broader than simply standing in front of a classroom and teaching English. Participants can become involved in different educational and cultural activities depending on the needs of their school or Contracting Organisation.

Typical responsibilities may include the following.

1. Assisting with foreign-language classes

ALTs assist Japanese teachers with foreign-language lessons in elementary, junior high and senior high schools.

This can involve supporting classroom activities, language practice, communication exercises and other activities designed to help students develop their foreign-language abilities.

The exact nature of classroom involvement may depend on the school, teaching arrangements and instructions provided by the relevant supervisor.

2. Supporting foreign-language activities in elementary schools

Participants may also assist with foreign-language activities for younger learners.

This gives ALTs an opportunity to introduce language learning in engaging and accessible ways while interacting directly with Japanese pupils.

3. Helping prepare teaching materials

ALTs may contribute to the preparation of materials used for foreign-language education.

This could involve helping teachers develop language-learning resources or providing information and examples that support classroom instruction.

4. Supporting language training for teachers

Participants may assist with language training for Japanese teachers of foreign languages or other language-related activities.

Their perspective as international participants can be useful in providing practical language knowledge and insights into how English and other foreign languages are used.

5. Participating in extracurricular and club activities

The JET Programme can extend beyond formal classroom instruction.

ALTs may cooperate with extracurricular activities and school clubs, allowing them to interact with students in less formal educational environments.

6. Providing language-related information

Participants may provide information to teachers and language consultants on matters such as:

  • Word usage
  • Pronunciation
  • Language expressions
  • Other language-related subjects

This responsibility allows participants to contribute their knowledge of their own language and culture to the Japanese education system.

7. Supporting foreign-language speech contests

ALTs may also assist with foreign-language speech contests.

This could include helping students prepare, providing language-related guidance or supporting the organisation of such activities, depending on the requirements of the school or Contracting Organisation.

8. Supporting local international exchange activities

One of the most important elements of the JET Programme is international exchange.

Participants may cooperate in local international exchange activities, helping communities develop greater awareness and understanding of other countries and cultures.

9. Performing other duties as required

Participants may be assigned additional duties considered necessary by their supervisor or school principal.

Because assignments differ between Contracting Organisations, applicants should understand that the precise responsibilities of an ALT can vary.

Where Do JET Participants Work?

JET participants are generally appointed by Japanese prefectures, municipalities, private schools and other Contracting Organisations.

This means that successful applicants are not necessarily assigned to one specific city or region in Japan. Their eventual placement depends on the organisation to which they are appointed.

Participants can therefore expect their experience to be shaped partly by their assigned community, school and local working environment.

For someone interested in experiencing Japanese life beyond major tourist destinations, this aspect of the programme can be particularly significant because placements can connect participants with local communities and educational institutions.

One-Year Participation Period

Participants are generally appointed for a one-year period.

The programme is therefore designed as a substantial international experience rather than a short-term visit. Successful applicants should be prepared to live and work in Japan for the duration of their appointment.

The Embassy of Japan also emphasises that participants should avoid withdrawing from the programme after receiving an assignment or ending their participation early, as doing so can create significant difficulties for the Contracting Organisation and affect the administration of the programme.

Applicants should therefore consider the commitment carefully before applying.

Financial Support and Transportation

According to the Embassy of Japan’s information, the cost of transportation from the participant’s place of origin to Japan, as well as remuneration, is funded by Japanese taxpayers through the Contracting Organisation where the participant is appointed.

This means successful participants receive financial support connected to their participation and employment under the programme.

Because participants serve as staff members of their respective Contracting Organisations, they are expected to observe applicable rules and behave responsibly.

The financial arrangements therefore form part of a broader employment and public-service structure rather than being simply a study-abroad scholarship.

Professional and Personal Development Opportunities

The JET Programme can provide participants with an opportunity to develop skills that extend beyond language education.

Living and working in another country can expose participants to new professional environments, educational systems and cultural practices.

Participants can potentially develop experience in areas such as:

  • Classroom support and education
  • Public speaking and communication
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Community engagement
  • International relations
  • Cultural exchange
  • Teamwork
  • Adaptability
  • Interpersonal communication
  • Working in a foreign professional environment
  • Understanding Japanese society and culture

For graduates interested in careers involving international development, education, communications, diplomacy, international organisations, cultural exchange or global affairs, such experience can provide useful exposure.

Expectations of JET Participants

JET participants are regarded as representatives of their respective countries.

The Embassy of Japan therefore stresses the importance of responsible behaviour and mutual understanding.

Applicants should understand that the programme is not solely about travelling to Japan. Participants are expected to make a meaningful contribution to the communities in which they live and work.

The Embassy indicates that desirable participants should be:

  • Adaptable
  • Mentally capable of performing their duties
  • Physically capable of performing their duties
  • Deeply interested in Japan
  • Responsible in their activities
  • Committed to promoting mutual understanding between nations

Participants should therefore be prepared to adapt to a different cultural and professional environment.

Why the International Exchange Element Matters

International exchange is central to the JET Programme.

An ALT from South Africa, for example, does more than assist with language education. Their presence can give Japanese students and community members opportunities to learn about South Africa and interact with someone from a different cultural background.

At the same time, the participant gains first-hand exposure to Japanese culture and society.

This two-way exchange is one of the fundamental purposes of the programme.

Participants are encouraged to build relationships with the communities where they are placed, contributing to a broader international network that can continue beyond their period in Japan.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to young South African university graduates who are interested in combining professional experience with international cultural exchange.

Potentially suitable applicants may include graduates interested in:

  • Teaching and education
  • English-language education
  • International exchange
  • Japanese culture
  • International development
  • Global communication
  • Community engagement
  • Cross-cultural relations
  • International careers

Applicants should also be comfortable with the responsibilities associated with representing their country in an international programme.

Application Deadline for JET Programme 2027

The deadline is 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026.

Importantly, applications must arrive at the Embassy of Japan by the deadline. Applicants should therefore not wait until the final day to send their documents.

The Embassy specifically instructs applicants to either courier their complete application package with a tracking number or hand deliver it to the designated address.

Application address

Embassy of Japan
JET Programme
259 Baines Street
Groenkloof
Pretoria
0181
South Africa

Applicants using courier services should allow sufficient time for the package to arrive before the stated deadline.

How to Apply for the JET Programme 2027

Applicants should carefully review the official JET Programme information and application documentation before preparing their submissions.

The basic submission process indicated by the Embassy is:

  1. Review the official JET Programme information and application requirements.
  2. Complete the required application documentation.
  3. Prepare the complete application package.
  4. Check that all required documents have been included.
  5. Submit the package by courier with a tracking number or hand deliver it to the Embassy of Japan in Pretoria.
  6. Ensure that the application arrives by 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026.
  7. Wait for notification by email regarding the outcome of the application.

Applicants should ensure that their submissions are complete and comply with the instructions in the official application documentation.

Selection Results

The Embassy of Japan states that both successful and unsuccessful applicants will be contacted by email.

Applicants are specifically requested not to contact the Embassy to enquire about the outcome of their application.

It is therefore important for applicants to monitor the email address provided in their application after submission.

To APPLY download the application form HERE.

Important Considerations Before Applying

The JET Programme can be a major international and professional opportunity, but applicants should understand the commitment involved.

Before applying, prospective participants should consider whether they are prepared to:

  • Live in Japan for at least one year.
  • Adapt to a different cultural and social environment.
  • Work within the Japanese education system.
  • Follow the instructions of their supervisors and Contracting Organisations.
  • Interact professionally with students, teachers and community members.
  • Represent South Africa responsibly.
  • Participate actively in international and cultural exchange.
  • Accept the responsibilities associated with their assigned position.
  • Commit to the programme rather than treating it simply as an opportunity for travel.

The programme is intended for individuals who can make a meaningful contribution while adapting to life and work in Japan.

Visit HERE to learn more about the JET Programme 2027.

Conclusion

The JET Programme 2027 offers young South African university graduates an opportunity to spend at least one year in Japan while working as Assistant Language Teachers and contributing to international exchange.

The programme combines language education, professional experience, community engagement and cultural exchange. Participants can work alongside Japanese teachers and educational authorities, support foreign-language classes, assist with teaching materials and extracurricular activities, contribute to speech contests and participate in local international exchange initiatives.

Beyond the professional responsibilities, the programme provides an opportunity to experience Japanese society from within a local community while helping Japanese students and residents learn more about South Africa and the wider world.

Interested South African graduates should begin preparing their applications well before the deadline. The complete application package must arrive at the Embassy of Japan in Pretoria no later than 4:00 PM on 16 October 2026.

For the official application instructions, detailed information and application forms, applicants should consult the Embassy of Japan in South Africa’s official JET Programme information before submitting their documents.

item.content:encoded:
The Niu Lab at New Mexico State University (NMSU) is inviting applications from highly motivated prospective PhD students interested in advancing the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, computer vision and related technologies in agriculture. The fully funded PhD positions provide an opportunity for students to undertake interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and agricultural applications, with an anticipated start in Spring or Fall 2027.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for graduates in computer science, engineering, agricultural engineering and closely related disciplines who want to pursue advanced research focused on developing intelligent technologies for productive and sustainable agriculture.

According to the opportunity announcement, the Niu Lab is recruiting multiple PhD students to join NMSU’s Department of Computer Science and work across artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics and agriculture.

Overview of the PhD Opportunity

The positions are hosted by the Niu Lab at New Mexico State University and will be supervised by Dr. Haoyu Niu. The selected PhD students will conduct research in an interdisciplinary environment, working with several NMSU units and agricultural research partners.

The research brings together computer science and agricultural applications, creating opportunities for students to work on technologies capable of addressing real-world challenges in modern agriculture.

The anticipated programme start is Spring or Fall 2027, depending on the position and successful applicant.

What Makes These PhD Positions Fully Funded?

One of the major advantages of the opportunity is that each position comes with several forms of financial and academic support.

Successful PhD students will receive:

  • A stipend to support their graduate studies and living expenses.
  • Tuition coverage, helping reduce the financial burden associated with pursuing a doctoral degree.
  • Health insurance as part of the funding package.
  • Conference travel support, providing opportunities for students to participate in academic and research conferences and share their work with the wider scientific community.

The attached announcement specifically states that each position includes a stipend, tuition coverage, health insurance and conference travel support.

This combination makes the opportunity particularly attractive to students seeking a funded doctoral research pathway in artificial intelligence, robotics, computer vision and agricultural technology.

Research Areas Covered by the PhD Positions

The PhD positions focus on several closely connected areas of artificial intelligence and agricultural technology. Applicants are expected to have an academic background or strong research interest in at least one of the listed areas.

1. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

Students may conduct research involving:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Deep learning
  • Reinforcement learning

These areas can be applied to agricultural problems requiring intelligent prediction, analysis, automation and decision-making.

Applicants with previous research experience in AI or machine learning are therefore well positioned to demonstrate their suitability for the positions.

2. Computer Vision and Multimodal Sensing

Another major research area is computer vision and multimodal sensing.

This area is relevant to agricultural systems that need to collect and interpret visual or other forms of sensor information. Students interested in using cameras, sensors and AI-based analysis to understand agricultural environments may find this research direction particularly relevant.

3. Robotics and Autonomous Systems

The positions also cover robotics and autonomous systems, including:

  • Unmanned aerial vehicles
  • Unmanned ground vehicles
  • Autonomous navigation
  • Robotic agricultural applications

This research area provides opportunities to explore how intelligent machines can operate in agricultural environments with reduced human intervention.

4. Digital Twins and Agricultural Simulation

Another research direction is digital twins and simulation for agricultural systems.

Students working in this area may explore computational representations and simulations of agricultural systems as tools for research, analysis and decision-making.

The announcement identifies AI and machine learning, computer vision and multimodal sensing, robotics and autonomous systems, and digital twins and simulation for agricultural systems as key areas of research interest.

Interdisciplinary Research Environment

The PhD students will not work exclusively within one academic discipline.

Under the supervision of Dr. Haoyu Niu, students will collaborate with:

  • NMSU’s Institute for Applied Practice in AI and Machine Learning (IAAM)
  • The College of Agricultural, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences
  • The NMSU Agricultural Experiment Station
  • Researchers and collaborators working across artificial intelligence and agriculture

This interdisciplinary structure is important because the research is designed to connect advanced computational technologies with practical agricultural challenges.

Students will therefore have the opportunity to work at the intersection of technical research and agricultural applications rather than studying artificial intelligence in isolation.

Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should have an appropriate academic background and demonstrate an interest in research relevant to the positions.

Academic Qualifications

Applicants should hold a:

  • B.S. degree, or
  • M.S. degree

in one of the following areas:

  • Computer Science
  • Computer Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Electronic Engineering
  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Agricultural Engineering
  • A closely related field

The announcement specifically requires a B.S. or M.S. degree in one of these disciplines or a closely related area.

Research Background or Interest

Applicants should have an academic background or strong research interest in one or more of the following:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Deep learning
  • Reinforcement learning
  • Computer vision
  • Multimodal sensing
  • Robotics
  • Autonomous systems
  • Unmanned aerial vehicles
  • Unmanned ground vehicles
  • Digital twins
  • Agricultural systems simulation

Having relevant research experience can help demonstrate an applicant’s preparedness for doctoral-level research.

Programming Skills

Proficiency in C++ or Python is required for the positions.

Experience with ROS or ROS 2 is described as desirable.

This means applicants with programming experience in Python or C++, particularly those who have applied these skills to artificial intelligence, robotics, computer vision, machine learning or related research projects, may be well suited to the opportunity.

Applicants with experience using ROS or ROS 2 can also demonstrate additional preparation for research involving robotics and autonomous systems.

Willingness to Conduct Field Experiments

The PhD positions are not limited to laboratory or computer-based research.

Applicants must be willing to conduct field experiments. This requirement is particularly relevant because the research is connected to agriculture and may involve testing AI-enabled systems, sensing technologies, autonomous platforms or other technologies in real agricultural environments.

Prospective students should therefore be comfortable with an interdisciplinary research approach that may combine:

  1. Computational research;
  2. Programming and AI development;
  3. Data collection and analysis;
  4. Robotics or sensing technologies; and
  5. Agricultural field experiments.

Communication and Teamwork Skills

Applicants should also possess:

  • Strong written communication skills;
  • Strong oral communication skills; and
  • The ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary research team.

These skills are important for PhD researchers because doctoral research often involves collaboration with researchers from different academic backgrounds, presentation of findings, preparation of research publications and communication of technical results.

About the Principal Investigator

The positions are supervised by Dr. Haoyu Niu, who earned his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from the University of California, Merced, in 2022.

His research is focused on the intersection of:

  • Artificial intelligence;
  • Computer vision;
  • Autonomous robotics; and
  • Precision agriculture.

According to the announcement, his research has a particular focus on AI-enabled robotic systems for crop monitoring.

His work integrates:

  • Vision-based sensing;
  • Autonomous navigation;
  • Sensor fusion; and
  • Intelligent decision-making.

The overall objective is to develop practical technologies that can contribute to productive and sustainable agriculture.

This research profile makes the PhD positions particularly relevant to applicants who want to pursue careers in AI-enabled agriculture, agricultural robotics, precision agriculture, autonomous systems, computer vision or intelligent sensing.

How to Apply for the Fully Funded PhD Positions

Interested applicants are required to submit their application materials directly by email to Dr. Haoyu Niu.

Applicants should prepare the following:

1. Curriculum Vitae

Submit an updated CV highlighting relevant:

  • Academic qualifications;
  • Research experience;
  • Programming skills;
  • Publications;
  • Projects;
  • Technical skills; and
  • Other experience relevant to AI, robotics, computer vision, machine learning or agriculture.

2. Academic Transcripts

Applicants should provide their academic transcripts as part of the application.

These should demonstrate their academic preparation for doctoral-level research.

3. Samples of Relevant Work

Applicants should also provide samples demonstrating their previous research or technical work.

Examples specifically mentioned in the announcement include:

  • Publications;
  • Project reports; and
  • A portfolio.

Applicants should therefore select work that demonstrates their capabilities and research interests in areas relevant to the PhD positions.

The application materials should be emailed to Dr. Haoyu Niu at hniu@nmsu.edu.

Required Email Subject Line

Applicants should use the following format as the email subject:

“Your Name_PhD Application”

Using the requested subject line can help ensure that the application is clearly identified and processed appropriately.

Application Deadline

There is no fixed application deadline stated in the announcement.

Instead, applications will be reviewed as they are received until all positions are filled.

This makes early application particularly important. Interested candidates should prepare their materials and submit them as soon as possible rather than waiting for a conventional closing date.

Because positions may be filled progressively, applicants should not assume that applications submitted later will receive the same consideration as those submitted earlier.

APPLY HERE

Selection and Interview Process

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

After the initial review, shortlisted applicants will be invited to a virtual interview.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to discuss:

  • Their academic background;
  • Previous research experience;
  • Relevant programming skills;
  • Research interests;
  • Interest in AI and agriculture;
  • Relevant publications or projects;
  • Potential research directions; and
  • Their ability to work within an interdisciplinary research team.

Who Should Consider Applying?

These PhD positions may be particularly suitable for graduates who want to build advanced expertise in the application of artificial intelligence to agriculture.

Potential applicants include graduates interested in:

  • Artificial intelligence research;
  • Machine learning and deep learning;
  • Computer vision;
  • Robotics;
  • Autonomous systems;
  • Agricultural robotics;
  • Precision agriculture;
  • Multimodal sensing;
  • Digital twins;
  • Agricultural simulation;
  • Unmanned aerial vehicles;
  • Unmanned ground vehicles;
  • Intelligent agricultural systems; and
  • Sustainable and technology-driven agriculture.

The opportunity may also appeal to students who want to combine computer science or engineering with real-world agricultural applications.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable for Future Researchers

A doctoral position that combines AI with agriculture can provide an opportunity to work on research problems with practical applications.

Modern agriculture increasingly involves technologies such as sensors, robotics, computer vision, autonomous systems and data-driven decision-making. The Niu Lab’s research focus brings these technologies together with agricultural systems.

For students interested in this field, the opportunity offers several potentially valuable dimensions:

Fully Funded Doctoral Study

The funding package includes a stipend, tuition coverage, health insurance and conference travel support, reducing some of the financial challenges associated with doctoral education.

Exposure to Interdisciplinary Research

Students can work across computer science, AI, robotics and agricultural sciences, allowing them to develop expertise that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries.

Practical Agricultural Applications

The research is oriented toward practical technologies for agriculture, including crop monitoring, sensing, autonomous navigation and intelligent decision-making.

Conference Participation

Conference travel support can provide opportunities to present research and engage with researchers working in related fields.

Advanced Technical Research

Students can develop research expertise in areas such as deep learning, computer vision, robotics, autonomous systems, sensor fusion and agricultural simulation.

Anticipated Start Date

The positions are expected to begin in:

  • Spring 2027, or
  • Fall 2027

The exact start timing may depend on the position and successful applicant.

Application Checklist

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should ensure that they have:

  1. An updated CV.
  2. Academic transcripts.
  3. Relevant publications, project reports or portfolio materials.
  4. Evidence of relevant AI, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, engineering or agricultural research experience where applicable.
  5. Demonstrated proficiency in C++ or Python.
  6. A clear explanation of their research interests.
  7. An interest in interdisciplinary research.
  8. Willingness to conduct agricultural field experiments.
  9. The correct email subject line: Your Name_PhD Application.
  10. All materials ready for submission to hniu@nmsu.edu.

Visit HERE for more information about the Fully Funded PhD Positions in AI for Agriculture at New Mexico State University, USA.

Conclusion

The Fully Funded PhD Positions in AI for Agriculture at New Mexico State University offer an opportunity for qualified graduates to pursue doctoral research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics and agriculture.

With funding that includes a stipend, tuition coverage, health insurance and conference travel support, the positions are designed to support students throughout their doctoral research. The programme also provides an interdisciplinary environment involving computer science and agricultural research, with research directions ranging from deep learning and computer vision to autonomous robotics, multimodal sensing, digital twins and agricultural simulation.

The positions are expected to begin in Spring or Fall 2027, while applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis until all positions are filled. Prospective applicants should therefore prepare their CV, transcripts and relevant work samples and submit their application directly to Dr. Haoyu Niu as early as possible.

item.content:encoded:
The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme 2027 is inviting nominations for the next generation of high-potential African leaders who are expected to take on significant leadership roles and contribute to Africa’s transformation over the coming years.

Organised by the African Leadership Institute (AFLI), the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship is the organisation’s flagship leadership development programme. The programme has been offered since 2006 and is designed to identify, develop and connect promising young African leaders across different sectors of society.

For the Class of 2027, approximately 25 high-potential individuals from across Africa will ultimately be selected through a rigorous and competitive process. However, unlike many fellowship programmes, individuals cannot directly apply or nominate themselves. Candidates must first be nominated by another person and, following the nomination and screening stages, eligible nominees will be invited to complete the full fellowship application.

The programme is designed for Africans between 30 and 39 years of age who demonstrate strong leadership potential and the capacity to contribute meaningfully to Africa’s social, economic and political transformation.

Nomination deadline for the Class of 2027: September 20, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time.

The subsequent candidate application process is scheduled to begin around September 25, 2026, with applications and letters of recommendation due by October 25, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg time.

About the African Leadership Institute

The African Leadership Institute (AFLI) is focused on nurturing and strengthening leadership capabilities across Africa, particularly among young people who demonstrate exceptional leadership potential.

The Institute’s broader objective is to develop a network of high-potential African leaders who can progress into senior leadership positions within their respective fields over the following five to ten years.

AFLI seeks to develop leaders who will not only advance professionally but also remain actively engaged in creating positive change across Africa.

The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship is the Institute’s flagship programme through which it pursues this objective.

The fellowship has been running since 2006, creating a network of alumni who have participated in leadership learning and development activities designed to strengthen their experiences, insights, leadership tools and confidence.

What Is the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship?

The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme is a prestigious leadership development programme aimed at identifying and developing the next generation of African leaders.

Each year, approximately 25 high-potential individuals from across Africa are selected following a rigorous competitive selection process.

The programme targets individuals who are expected to become influential leaders in their respective fields over the next five to ten years.

Importantly, the fellowship is not limited to one profession or sector.

The programme is intended for emerging leaders across all sectors of African society, meaning that candidates can come from different professional, social, economic, public, private, civil society and other leadership backgrounds.

The central question is not simply what sector an individual works in, but whether the person demonstrates the leadership potential, experience and commitment necessary to contribute to Africa’s transformation.

The Purpose of the Tutu Fellowship

The fellowship is designed around the idea that Africa’s future depends significantly on the development of capable, ethical and transformative leaders.

AFLI therefore seeks individuals who have already demonstrated leadership potential and who can develop into influential leaders in their respective fields.

Through the fellowship, selected participants receive leadership learning activities intended to strengthen:

  • Leadership experience
  • Strategic insight
  • Personal confidence
  • Leadership tools
  • Understanding of complex African challenges
  • Capacity to influence positive change
  • Professional networks
  • Collaboration across sectors and countries

The programme also seeks to create a lasting network of fellows who can support one another and contribute to Africa’s transformation beyond the fellowship itself.

Approximately 25 Fellows Will Be Selected

The Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is highly selective.

For each annual class, approximately 25 individuals are selected from across Africa.

This means that becoming a Tutu Fellow is a competitive achievement.

The programme describes its selected participants as some of the continent’s most promising future leaders and specifically targets individuals expected to rise into top leadership positions within their areas of activity over the next five to ten years.

Applicants and nominators should therefore understand that meeting the basic age and geographic requirements does not automatically result in selection.

The selection process is designed to identify candidates who demonstrate exceptional leadership potential and a strong capacity to contribute to the transformation of Africa.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The programme is designed for high-potential African leaders between 30 and 39 years of age.

The fellowship is not restricted to one professional discipline.

Potential candidates may come from sectors such as:

  • Government and public service
  • Business and entrepreneurship
  • Civil society
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Education
  • Academia and research
  • Media and communications
  • Technology
  • Finance
  • Development
  • Health
  • Law
  • Agriculture
  • Arts and culture
  • Social enterprise
  • Community development
  • International development
  • Other sectors of society

The key consideration is the candidate’s leadership potential and capacity to contribute to positive change.

Age Requirement for the Class of 2027

Candidates must be between:

30 and 39 years of age.

The nomination form explicitly requires the nominator to confirm the candidate’s age.

Applicants outside the specified age range should not be nominated for the programme.

Prospective candidates should therefore verify their age eligibility before approaching a potential nominator.

An Important Difference: You Cannot Apply Directly

One of the most important aspects of the Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is that direct applications are not accepted.

Individuals interested in becoming Tutu Fellows must first be nominated by another person.

This means:

  • You cannot nominate yourself.
  • You cannot submit a direct application without first being nominated.
  • You need someone else to put your name forward.
  • Only one nomination is necessary.
  • Multiple nominations may be regarded as abuse of the nomination process.

The programme specifically advises interested individuals who wish to be considered to read the relevant candidate guidance and seek nomination.

How the Nomination Process Works

The nomination process is designed to identify individuals who have demonstrated strong leadership potential.

A nominator must provide information about both themselves and the candidate.

The nomination form asks the nominator to provide:

  • Their name
  • Email address
  • Position or job title
  • How long they have known the candidate
  • The capacity in which they know the candidate
  • Confirmation that they have contacted the candidate
  • Confirmation that the candidate has given permission to be nominated

The nominator must therefore have some meaningful knowledge of the candidate.

The form provides different options for how long the nominator has known the candidate, including:

  • 1 year
  • 2 years
  • 2+ years
  • 5+ years
  • 10+ years

The form also asks the nominator to explain the capacity in which they know the candidate.

Click HERE to fill the nomination form.

Candidate Information Required During Nomination

The nomination form requires several details about the proposed candidate.

These include:

  1. Candidate’s first name
  2. Candidate’s last name
  3. Age
  4. Gender
  5. Nationality
  6. Country of residence
  7. Occupation
  8. Candidate’s personal email address
  9. Relevant information concerning inhibiting factors
  10. The nominator’s motivation for recommending the candidate

The candidate must therefore give the nominator permission to submit the nomination.

Candidate Permission Is Required

The nomination form specifically asks:

Has the nominator contacted the candidate and obtained permission to nominate them?

The available responses are:

  • Yes
  • No

This means individuals should not be nominated without their knowledge and permission.

Anyone considering nominating a colleague, professional contact, community leader or other person should first discuss the opportunity with that individual.

The Importance of the Nominator’s Motivation

One of the most significant parts of the nomination form is the section requiring the nominator to explain why the candidate would be a strong fit for the fellowship.

The programme specifically asks nominators to provide personal insight into the candidate rather than simply copying the person’s CV or biography.

The nominator is encouraged to address questions such as:

  • What makes this candidate a special and successful leader?
  • Why does the candidate stand out from other potential leaders?
  • What evidence demonstrates the candidate’s leadership ability?
  • How could the candidate’s leadership contribute to Africa’s transformation?
  • How could the candidate’s leadership contribute to improving the lives of people across the continent?

This section is limited to 2,700 characters.

Do Not Simply Copy the Candidate’s CV

The nomination guidance makes an important distinction between listing achievements and explaining why the person is an exceptional leadership candidate.

Nominators are specifically advised not to copy and paste the candidate’s CV or biography.

Instead, the nominator should provide personal insight that selectors would not obtain simply by reading a résumé.

This means the strongest nominations should explain the candidate’s leadership character, influence, achievements and potential in a compelling and personal way.

For example, a nominator could explain how they have observed the candidate:

  • Lead a difficult initiative
  • Mobilise communities
  • Solve complex problems
  • Influence institutional change
  • Build effective teams
  • Create employment or economic opportunities
  • Improve public services
  • Develop innovative solutions
  • Advocate for marginalised communities
  • Drive social or environmental change
  • Demonstrate ethical leadership

The objective is to help selectors understand the person behind the résumé.

Nationality and African Eligibility

The nomination form provides a comprehensive list of African countries and includes an option for candidates who were born outside Africa.

The African countries listed include:

  • Algeria
  • Angola
  • Benin
  • Botswana
  • Burkina Faso
  • Burundi
  • Cabo Verde

  • Malawi

  • Togo
  • Tunisia
  • Uganda
  • Zambia
  • Zimbabwe

The form’s inclusion of “Born out of Africa” is important for candidates whose circumstances require clarification concerning their place of birth and African nationality.

Prospective candidates should provide accurate nationality and residence information when being nominated.

Gender Eligibility

The nomination form provides the following gender options:

  • Male
  • Female
  • Non-binary

The inclusion of these options demonstrates that the nomination process is not presented as being limited to one gender.

The Selection Process for the Class of 2027

The Class of 2027 selection process follows several stages.

According to the updated AFLI schedule provided for the 2027 cycle, the process is structured approximately as follows.

Stage 1: Invited Nominations Open

August 26, 2026

Invited nominations for the Class of 2027 begin on August 26, 2026.

This marks the opening of the nomination stage through which prospective candidates can be put forward for consideration.

Stage 2: Nominations Close

September 20, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time

This is the critical deadline for nominations.

The nomination deadline is described as a hard deadline.

The nomination form will be taken down at the deadline and nominations submitted afterward will not be accepted.

Stage 3: Screening of Nominees

Following the nomination deadline, AFLI will screen the submitted nominees.

The screening process is expected to take approximately:

One week to 10 days after nominations close, depending on the number of nominations received.

Stage 4: Candidate Application Begins

The candidate application process is expected to begin:

On or around September 25, 2026.

Candidates who progress through the nomination and screening stage will then be able to proceed with the formal fellowship application.

Stage 5: Candidate Application Deadline

The deadline for the full fellowship application is:

October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time.

This is separate from the September 20 nomination deadline.

Prospective candidates and their nominators should therefore understand that there are two important deadlines:

  • September 20, 2026: nomination deadline
  • October 25, 2026: candidate application deadline

Stage 6: Recommendation Letter Deadline

Letters of recommendation from referees are also due by:

October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time.

Candidates should therefore begin preparing their referees well in advance.

Stage 7: Selection Process Begins

The formal selection process is scheduled to begin in:

Early November 2026.

Stage 8: Shortlisted Candidates Informed

Shortlisted candidates are expected to be informed around:

Mid-December 2026.

Stage 9: Final Selection

The selectors are expected to finalise the Class of 2027 by:

Mid-January 2027.

Stage 10: Final Candidate Communication

Invitation emails are expected to be sent to Associates and Reserves beginning in:

February 2027.

Stage 11: Status of Applications

All candidates are expected to receive a status notification as the selection process progresses.

Most candidates are expected to receive status communications around November or December 2026, while finalists will receive status communication in early 2027.

Stage 12: Announcement of the Class of 2027

The Class of 2027 will be announced before the first programme workshop in South Africa.

The information provided does not give an exact announcement date.

The Nomination Deadline Is a Hard Deadline

A particularly important warning from AFLI concerns the nomination deadline.

The programme explicitly describes the deadline as a hard deadline.

This means candidates and nominators should not wait until the final hours to submit the nomination.

Technical problems can prevent a form from being successfully submitted.

The nomination guidance specifically warns against assuming that a last-minute submission will be successful.

Nominators are therefore encouraged to submit their nominations well before the deadline.

Why Early Submission Matters

Online application systems can experience problems for many reasons, including:

  • Slow internet connections
  • Browser problems
  • Server congestion
  • Incorrect information
  • Form errors
  • Difficulty uploading information
  • Connectivity interruptions

Because the nomination deadline is hard, a technical problem occurring shortly before midnight does not necessarily result in an extension.

The programme therefore advises nominators to submit early.

The Role of Referees

For candidates who progress to the formal application stage, letters of recommendation are an important component of the selection process.

The deadline for recommendation letters for the Class of 2027 is:

October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg time.

Candidates should therefore identify appropriate referees early and make sure they understand the deadline.

A candidate should ideally select people who can provide meaningful evidence of their leadership, professional achievements, character and potential.

Leadership Potential Is Central to the Fellowship

The Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is specifically aimed at the next generation of African leaders.

Therefore, simply having a successful career may not be enough.

Candidates should be able to demonstrate evidence of leadership potential.

This may include:

  • Leading organisations
  • Building successful businesses
  • Driving institutional reforms
  • Developing innovative initiatives
  • Leading social movements
  • Creating community programmes
  • Influencing policy
  • Building partnerships
  • Improving systems
  • Mentoring others
  • Advancing social justice
  • Promoting economic development
  • Addressing environmental challenges
  • Creating opportunities for other people

The strongest candidates are likely to be individuals whose leadership extends beyond personal advancement and demonstrates wider social value.

Contribution to Africa’s Transformation

AFLI’s nomination form specifically asks how a candidate’s leadership will contribute to the transformation of Africa and improve the lives of people on the continent.

This makes the candidate’s broader vision particularly important.

A prospective candidate should be able to articulate:

  • What major challenge they are addressing
  • Why the challenge matters
  • What they have already done
  • What impact they have achieved
  • What they hope to accomplish in the future
  • How their leadership can contribute to broader African development

The emphasis should be on measurable or observable impact wherever possible.

The Fellowship Is Not Limited to One Career Path

One of the strengths of the Archbishop Tutu Fellowship is its cross-sector approach.

The programme seeks future leaders from all sectors of society.

This means that a candidate does not necessarily need to work in government, politics or international development.

A leader in business, technology, education, health, civil society, entrepreneurship, media, agriculture, science or another sector can potentially be considered.

What matters is the combination of leadership potential, achievement, vision and commitment to positive change.

The Fellowship’s Leadership Network

AFLI aims to create a network of high-potential African leaders who have participated in its programmes.

The purpose of this network is to connect individuals who are expected to move into significant leadership positions over the next five to ten years.

This network can provide an environment in which fellows can exchange ideas, develop relationships and collaborate across countries and professional sectors.

The fellowship therefore has a longer-term objective that extends beyond the immediate programme activities.

What Does the Programme Aim to Develop?

The leadership learning activities are designed to strengthen selected candidates’:

  • Experiences
  • Insights
  • Leadership tools
  • Confidence
  • Professional and leadership networks
  • Capacity to drive transformation

The programme seeks to give participants practical leadership resources that they can apply within their organisations, communities and wider societies.

Preparing for the Tutu Fellowship Nomination

If you are a prospective candidate, the first step is not to complete an application yourself.

Instead, you should identify an appropriate person who can nominate you.

Potential nominators could include people who know your work and leadership closely, depending on their relationship with you.

Before asking someone to nominate you, consider whether they can genuinely explain:

  • How they know you
  • What leadership they have observed
  • What makes you exceptional
  • What impact you have made
  • Why you have the potential to become a major African leader

A nomination from someone who knows your work deeply is likely to provide more meaningful insight than a nomination from someone who knows you only superficially.

What Makes a Strong Nomination?

A strong nomination should tell a convincing leadership story.

It should answer questions such as:

What problem has the candidate addressed?

Describe the challenge or opportunity that motivated the candidate’s leadership.

What did the candidate do?

Explain the candidate’s specific role rather than describing a collective achievement without identifying the individual’s contribution.

What changed because of the candidate’s leadership?

Where possible, provide evidence of outcomes.

Why is the candidate different?

Explain what distinguishes the person from other capable professionals.

What could the candidate achieve in the future?

Describe the candidate’s future leadership potential and how it could contribute to Africa.

The Importance of Impact

Impact is an important concept throughout the fellowship’s nomination process.

Candidates should therefore consider the difference their leadership has made.

Impact can take many forms, including:

  • People reached
  • Jobs created
  • Policies influenced
  • Organisations transformed
  • Communities served
  • Innovations introduced
  • Educational outcomes improved
  • Health outcomes improved
  • Environmental benefits
  • Economic opportunities created
  • Young people mentored
  • Women and marginalised communities empowered

The relevant evidence will depend on the candidate’s sector.

Click HERE to learn more about the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship.

Application Guidance and Official Resources

Prospective nominators and candidates should review the official AFLI resources before participating in the process.

Useful resources include:

  • Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship Programme
  • Guidelines for Candidates
  • Guidelines for Nominators
  • Guidelines for Selectors
  • Key Dates and Deadlines
  • AFLI Contact Page
  • African Leadership Institute

The official programme website also provides information about subscribing to the AFLI mailing list for announcements concerning the fellowship and other AFLI programmes.

Important Application and Nomination Tips

Prospective candidates and nominators should keep the following points in mind:

  1. Do not self-nominate. Direct applications and self-nominations are not accepted.
  2. Secure permission first. A candidate should know about and approve their nomination.
  3. Read the nomination guidance carefully.
  4. Submit the nomination early. The September 20 deadline is a hard deadline.
  5. Do not submit multiple nominations. The programme states that only one nomination is necessary and multiple nominations may be considered abuse.
  6. Choose a knowledgeable nominator. The person should be able to provide meaningful insight into the candidate’s leadership.
  7. Prepare for the formal application. Candidates who progress beyond screening should be ready to complete the next stage quickly.
  8. Choose referees early. Recommendation letters have a firm October 25 deadline.
  9. Focus on impact. Demonstrate what your leadership has changed.
  10. Think beyond personal achievement. Explain how your leadership contributes to Africa’s transformation.

Key Dates for the Archbishop Tutu Fellowship Class of 2027

Stage Date
Invited nominations open August 26, 2026
Nominations close September 20, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg time
Screening of nominees Approximately 1–10 days after nomination closure
Candidate application begins On or around September 25, 2026
Candidate application deadline October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg time
Recommendation letter deadline October 25, 2026 at midnight Johannesburg time
Selection process begins Early November 2026
Shortlisted candidates informed Mid-December 2026
Class finalisation Mid-January 2027
Final candidate communications Beginning February 2027
Class of 2027 announcement Before the first workshop

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship?

It is the flagship leadership development programme of the African Leadership Institute, designed to identify and develop high-potential African leaders who are expected to contribute to the continent’s transformation.

How many people are selected?

Approximately 25 individuals are selected for each annual class.

What age group is eligible?

Candidates must be between 30 and 39 years old.

Can I apply directly?

No. Direct applications and self-nominations are not accepted. A candidate must first be nominated by another person.

Can I receive more than one nomination?

Only one nomination is necessary. The programme warns that multiple nominations may be considered abuse.

Do I need to be living in Africa?

The information provided includes nationality and country-of-residence fields and lists African nationalities. Prospective candidates should carefully review the official candidate guidance if their nationality, residence or place of birth creates a special circumstance.

Is the fellowship limited to one profession?

No. The programme targets future leaders across all sectors of African society.

How many years has the fellowship been running?

The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship has been offered since 2006.

When is the nomination deadline?

For the Class of 2027, nominations close on September 20, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg, South Africa time.

When does the full application begin?

The application process is expected to begin on or around September 25, 2026, following screening of nominees.

When is the full application deadline?

The deadline for applications and letters of recommendation is October 25, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg time.

When will the Class of 2027 be announced?

The Class of 2027 will be announced before the first workshop in South Africa. The information provided does not specify an exact announcement date.

Visit HERE to read the Full FAQs.

Final Checklist for Prospective Candidates

Before seeking nomination, prospective candidates should ask themselves:

  • Am I between 30 and 39 years old?
  • Am I an African national or otherwise eligible under AFLI’s nationality requirements?
  • Can I demonstrate significant leadership experience or potential?
  • Have I contributed to positive change?
  • Can I explain how my leadership contributes to Africa’s transformation?
  • Am I prepared to commit to the fellowship process?
  • Do I know someone who can provide a strong and genuine nomination?
  • Have I discussed the nomination with that person?
  • Can my nominator provide personal insight rather than simply copying my CV?
  • Have I reviewed the official fellowship guidance?
  • Am I prepared for the subsequent application process if I am shortlisted?

Conclusion

The Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship 2027 represents a major leadership development opportunity for high-potential Africans who are already demonstrating the capacity to influence their organisations, communities, sectors and societies.

Run by the African Leadership Institute, the fellowship has been offered since 2006 and seeks to build a network of emerging African leaders who are expected to rise into significant leadership positions over the next five to ten years.

For the Class of 2027, approximately 25 individuals will be selected through a rigorous process. The programme is open to emerging leaders across sectors rather than being restricted to a particular profession. Candidates must be between 30 and 39 years old and must first be nominated by another person.

The most important point for prospective candidates is that there is no direct application route. Interested individuals must secure a nomination, and only one nomination is necessary. Candidates should therefore identify someone who knows their leadership and achievements well enough to provide a compelling and personal assessment of their potential.

The nomination deadline is September 20, 2026, at midnight Johannesburg time. Candidates who successfully progress through the nomination and screening stage are expected to begin the formal application process around September 25, with the application and recommendation-letter deadline set for October 25, 2026.

Because the nomination deadline is a hard deadline, prospective nominators should begin early and avoid submitting at the last minute. A strong nomination should go beyond repeating a candidate’s CV and should clearly explain what makes the candidate an exceptional leader, what impact they have already created and how their future leadership could contribute to the transformation of Africa.

For African professionals and emerging leaders who meet the age requirements and have a demonstrated record of leadership, service and positive impact, the Archbishop Tutu Leadership Fellowship offers an opportunity to join a network specifically focused on developing the continent’s next generation of influential leaders.

Discover more global Fellowship, Leadership Development and African opportunities on OFY.
