item.content:encoded:
The United Nations University (UNU) is inviting applications for a Remote Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education position at the UNU Institute in Macau (UNU Macau). This two-month research internship provides an opportunity for qualified postgraduate researchers to gain practical experience in policy-oriented research while contributing to work examining the intersection of neuroscience, learning sciences, artificial intelligence and higher education.

The internship is particularly relevant for candidates with an academic background in neuroscience, education, learning sciences, psychology, artificial intelligence, social sciences or a related discipline who are interested in understanding how emerging technologies and evidence from learning and neuroscience can influence education policy and practice.

The successful intern will work remotely under the supervision of the Institute Director and contribute to research for a forthcoming Springer publication on AI and higher education, alongside research briefs, policy recommendations, blogs, academic papers and other knowledge products.

Financial Support

The advertised position lists a payment of $550 per month.

Duration

The internship will last for 2 months.

The anticipated internship period is:

  • Start date: October 5, 2026
  • End date: December 4, 2026

Application Deadline

September 18, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Macau time (GMT+8).

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline because the application page will no longer be operational after the closing date.

About the United Nations University

The United Nations University is an international community of scholars working on policy-oriented research, capacity development and knowledge dissemination in support of the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter.

For more than four decades, UNU has served as a global research and think-tank institution working on major challenges affecting human survival, conflict prevention, sustainable development and human welfare.

Its research contributes to the broader work of the United Nations and its Member States and covers issues connected to the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

UNU brings together researchers working across different countries and disciplines. The university also maintains collaborations with United Nations agencies, universities and research institutions around the world.

This makes a UNU internship particularly valuable for individuals seeking exposure to international research, evidence-based policymaking, sustainable development and the United Nations system.

About UNU Institute in Macau

The United Nations University Institute in Macau is one of the research and training institutes within the UNU system.

UNU Macau focuses on the relationship between digital technologies and sustainable development, undertaking research designed to address challenges identified within the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

The Institute emphasizes:

  • Digital technology and sustainable development
  • Evidence-based policymaking
  • Data-driven approaches
  • Applied research
  • Innovation and emerging technologies
  • ICT for development
  • Interdisciplinary research
  • Policy impact at international, regional and national levels

One of the Institute’s objectives is to help nurture the next generation of interdisciplinary researchers, including computing, information and social scientists and engineers working in ICT for development.

The Institute’s location in Macau also places it within the broader Greater Bay Area, a major technology and innovation hub with connections to China, Hong Kong SAR and several other Asian countries.

For the selected intern, this provides an opportunity to participate in research connected to major technological and educational developments while working within a United Nations research environment.

About the Research Internship

The Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education will support ongoing research under the supervision of the Institute Director.

The internship is connected to a forthcoming Springer publication on artificial intelligence and higher education, meaning the successful candidate will have an opportunity to contribute to research that may ultimately inform an academic publication.

The role combines several areas of expertise, including:

  1. Neuroscience
  2. Learning science
  3. Education
  4. Artificial intelligence
  5. Higher education
  6. Social science research
  7. Education policy
  8. Academic writing
  9. Knowledge translation
  10. Evidence-based policymaking

The position is therefore well suited to candidates who enjoy interdisciplinary research and are interested in translating academic evidence into practical policy and educational recommendations.

Key Responsibilities

The selected Research Intern will undertake a range of research and knowledge-production activities.

1. Conduct Literature Reviews

A major responsibility will involve conducting literature reviews and research relating to:

  • Neuroscience
  • Learning
  • Education
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Higher education

The intern will be expected to identify relevant academic literature, examine existing evidence, synthesize findings and help establish an evidence base for ongoing UNU research.

Strong literature-review skills will therefore be important because the role requires the ability to navigate academic research and identify information relevant to specific research questions.

2. Support Research for the Springer Book

The intern will support research and analysis contributing to a forthcoming Springer book focused on AI and higher education.

This could involve reviewing academic literature, organizing research materials, synthesizing findings and supporting the development of content for the publication.

The opportunity may therefore be particularly attractive to candidates who want experience contributing to an international academic publication.

3. Explore Neuroscience and Learning Science

The intern will examine how findings and insights from neuroscience and learning science can contribute to better educational policies and practices.

This involves exploring the relationship between how people learn, what research says about learning and cognition, and how these insights can be incorporated into education systems.

The role therefore goes beyond simply studying artificial intelligence. It requires an interdisciplinary understanding of how AI, learning, neuroscience and education intersect.

4. Contribute to Education Policy Recommendations

Another important responsibility will be contributing to policy outputs and recommendations.

The intern will explore how evidence from neuroscience and learning science can potentially inform policymaking within education.

This may include helping translate academic findings into practical recommendations that policymakers and other stakeholders can understand and potentially apply.

5. Write Blogs and Research Publications

The selected candidate will also contribute to various written knowledge products.

These may include:

  • Blog articles
  • Research papers
  • Journal articles
  • Policy outputs
  • Other knowledge products

This means candidates should be comfortable communicating complex academic information clearly and accurately.

Strong academic and analytical writing will be particularly important for this aspect of the internship.

6. Prepare and Analyze Research Materials

The intern will assist with the preparation, organization and analysis of research materials and evidence.

This responsibility requires attention to detail and the ability to work systematically with academic information.

Expected Outputs

During the internship, the successful candidate is expected to contribute to several research and knowledge products.

These include:

Research Briefs and Literature Reviews

The intern may contribute to research briefs and comprehensive literature reviews examining neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education.

Policy Recommendations

The intern will contribute to recommendations examining how neuroscience and learning science can be incorporated into educational policymaking.

Blog Articles and Public-Facing Content

The internship also provides an opportunity to contribute to blogs and other materials designed to communicate research findings to broader audiences.

Academic Publications

The intern may contribute to drafts or research supporting journal articles and other academic publications.

Springer Book Research

A significant component of the internship will involve research and analysis contributing to the forthcoming Springer book on artificial intelligence and higher education.

Learning Opportunities and Professional Development

The internship is designed not only to support UNU’s research activities but also to provide professional development for the selected intern.

1. Strengthen Research Skills

Interns will gain practical experience conducting research in a professional international research environment.

This can strengthen abilities in:

  • Literature reviews
  • Evidence synthesis
  • Research analysis
  • Academic writing
  • Research organization
  • Knowledge production

2. Learn to Translate Research Into Policy

One of the most valuable learning objectives is developing the ability to transform research findings into policy-relevant outputs.

This is particularly useful for individuals interested in careers involving:

  • Public policy
  • International development
  • Education policy
  • Research
  • Think tanks
  • Academia
  • International organizations
  • Technology policy

3. Gain United Nations Experience

The internship provides exposure to the working environment of the United Nations University.

Experience within a UN institution can help candidates better understand how international organizations conduct research, generate evidence and contribute to global policy discussions.

4. Work in a Multicultural Environment

UNU operates within an international and multicultural environment.

The internship therefore offers an opportunity to develop experience collaborating across different cultural, academic and professional backgrounds.

Required Qualifications

Applicants must meet the academic and professional requirements outlined for the position.

Educational Requirements

Candidates must have a Master’s degree or higher in one of the following areas:

  • Neuroscience
  • Education
  • Learning sciences
  • Psychology
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Social sciences
  • A related field

The interdisciplinary nature of the position means that candidates from different academic backgrounds may be considered, provided their expertise is relevant to the research focus.

Required Skills and Experience

Applicants should demonstrate strong capabilities in research and academic writing.

Key requirements include:

Strong Research Skills

Candidates should have experience conducting structured and rigorous research.

Analytical Skills

The position requires the ability to analyze academic evidence, identify important findings and synthesize information.

Academic Writing

Applicants should be capable of producing clear, well-structured academic and research-oriented writing.

Literature Review Experience

Candidates should demonstrate the ability to conduct literature reviews and synthesize findings from academic research.

Interest in Interdisciplinary Research

Applicants should have a strong interest in the intersection of:

Neuroscience + Learning + Artificial Intelligence + Higher Education

Ability to Work Independently

Because the position is remote, applicants must be able to organize their workload, manage deadlines and work effectively with limited direct supervision.

Language Requirements

Candidates must have:

  • Excellent written English
  • Excellent spoken English

Knowledge of another United Nations official language is considered an advantage.

Applicants who can demonstrate multilingual communication skills may therefore have an additional strength, although English proficiency is the primary language requirement specified for the position.

Core Values and Competencies

The internship follows UNU’s core values and competency framework.

Core Values

Candidates are expected to demonstrate:

  • Respect for diversity
  • Integrity
  • Professionalism

Core Competencies

The position also emphasizes:

  • Awareness and sensitivity regarding gender issues
  • Accountability
  • Creative problem solving
  • Effective communication
  • Inclusive collaboration

Applicants should consider demonstrating these competencies through their cover letter, CV and examples of previous research or professional work.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is open to qualified candidates who meet the stated academic and skills requirements.

Applicants should have:

  • A Master’s degree or above
  • A background in neuroscience, education, learning sciences, psychology, AI, social sciences or a related field
  • Strong research and analytical abilities
  • Strong academic writing skills
  • Experience conducting literature reviews
  • An interest in neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education
  • The ability to work independently in a remote environment
  • Excellent written and spoken English

UNU specifically states that it welcomes applications regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic background, and encourages applications from persons living with disabilities.

The organization also strongly encourages applications from developing countries and women.

Therefore, the announcement does not restrict applicants to a particular continent or nationality. Qualified candidates from around the world can apply, subject to meeting the academic, skills and other requirements.

Application Requirements

Interested applicants must submit an application containing the following materials:

1. Cover Letter

Applicants should submit a brief cover letter written in English.

The cover letter should explain:

  • Why the applicant is interested in the internship
  • Their relevant qualifications
  • Their suitability for the research position
  • Their interest in neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education

The cover letter should be specifically tailored to the position rather than being a generic application letter.

2. Current CV

Applicants must submit a current and complete CV in English.

The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications or academic writing
  • Professional experience
  • Analytical skills
  • Relevant projects
  • Research interests

3. Examples of Relevant Research Work

Applicants must provide examples of relevant research work in English.

This could be particularly important because the internship is heavily research-focused. Candidates should therefore select examples that demonstrate their ability to conduct research, analyze evidence and communicate academic findings effectively.

Documents Required if Invited for an Interview

Candidates who are invited for an interview will be required to submit additional documentation before the interview.

These include:

Proof of Education Status

Applicants may provide documents such as:

  • Academic transcripts
  • Proof of enrollment
  • Other documents confirming their education status

Health and Life/Accident Insurance

Selected candidates must have health and life/accident insurance valid for the duration and location in which the internship is carried out.

This requirement should be taken seriously when preparing for the internship because the selected intern is responsible for having the required insurance coverage.

Selection and Assessment Process

UNU may assess qualified applicants through one or more stages.

The assessment process may include:

  1. Desk review of applications
  2. Competency-based interview
  3. Reference checks

Candidates should therefore prepare to discuss their academic background, research experience, analytical abilities, writing skills and motivation for joining UNU.

A competency-based interview may also explore examples of how candidates have demonstrated communication, accountability, problem solving, collaboration and other relevant competencies.

Important Information About the Remote Internship

The position is explicitly described as a remote internship.

This means applicants do not need to relocate to Macau to carry out the internship.

However, candidates should understand that remote work still requires:

  • Reliable communication
  • Independent time management
  • Consistent availability
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Strong written communication
  • Ability to collaborate virtually
  • Access to an appropriate working environment

Visa and Employment Considerations

UNU states that it does not sponsor a working visa for this position.

Because this is a remote internship, applicants should carefully consider the location from which they will undertake the internship and ensure they can legally participate from that location.

The internship is also intended to complement an intern’s studies and is not intended to lead directly to further employment with UNU.

Therefore, candidates should not regard the internship as a guaranteed pathway to a permanent or temporary position within the organization.

Status of Interns at UNU

Interns should also be aware that they do not have the same status as United Nations staff members.

According to the vacancy information:

  • Interns may not represent UNU in an official capacity.
  • Interns do not hold international civil servant status.
  • Interns are not considered staff members under the UN Staff Rules and Regulations.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between gaining experience through a UNU internship and being employed as a member of the United Nations international civil service.

Insurance and Personal Responsibility

UNU states that it accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents, illness or death incurred during the internship.

Selected interns must therefore ensure that they have the required health and life/accident insurance coverage for the relevant period.

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Researchers

This opportunity offers several potential benefits for postgraduate researchers and early-career professionals.

International Research Exposure

Working with a United Nations University institute can provide experience in an international research environment.

Interdisciplinary Experience

The internship brings together several rapidly developing fields, including artificial intelligence, neuroscience, learning sciences and higher education.

Academic Publication Experience

Contributing to research associated with a forthcoming Springer publication can provide valuable exposure to the academic publication process.

Policy Research Experience

The role emphasizes translating research into policy recommendations, making it relevant to candidates interested in evidence-based policymaking.

Writing and Knowledge Production

Interns can gain experience producing research briefs, blogs, academic papers and other knowledge products.

Remote International Collaboration

The position provides an opportunity to develop experience working remotely in an international and multicultural setting.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants can improve their applications by making sure every document directly reflects the requirements of the internship.

Tailor Your Cover Letter

Your cover letter should clearly connect your academic background and research experience to the internship’s focus.

Rather than simply stating that you are interested in AI or education, explain how your previous work relates to the intersection of neuroscience, learning, AI and higher education.

Highlight Research Experience

Your CV should make research experience easy to identify.

Include relevant:

  • Research projects
  • Literature reviews
  • Publications
  • Academic papers
  • Policy research
  • Research reports
  • Data analysis
  • Conferences or research presentations

Select Strong Writing Samples

Because academic writing is an important requirement, choose research samples that demonstrate your ability to synthesize evidence and communicate complex ideas clearly.

Demonstrate Independent Working Ability

Since this is a remote position, applicants should demonstrate examples of successfully managing research or professional responsibilities independently.

Show Policy-Relevant Thinking

Candidates can strengthen their application by demonstrating that they understand the importance of translating research into practical recommendations for policymakers, institutions and other stakeholders.

Application Deadline and Key Dates

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

  • Application deadline: September 18, 2026
  • Deadline time: 11:59 p.m. Macau time (GMT+8)
  • Expected start date: October 5, 2026
  • Expected end date: December 4, 2026
  • Duration: 2 months
  • Mode: Remote

Because the application page will no longer be operational after the deadline, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their materials.

Scam Warning

Applicants should be alert to recruitment scams.

UNU states that it does not charge application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other recruitment fees.

Applicants should therefore be cautious of anyone requesting payment in exchange for:

  • Application processing
  • Interview invitations
  • Recruitment
  • Training
  • Testing
  • Selection
  • Placement

Applicants should also be careful when providing personal information because organizational names, logos, addresses and other identifying information can be copied and misused by scammers.

Applications should be submitted through the official UNU recruitment platform.

Visit HERE for more information about the Remote Research Internship at United Nations University.

Application Link

Interested candidates should apply through the official United Nations University careers platform and carefully review the vacancy requirements before submitting their application.

Apply for the UNU Remote Research Internship

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The United Nations University Remote Research Internship in Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education offers an interdisciplinary research opportunity for Master’s-level and above candidates interested in the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence, neuroscience, learning and higher education.

The two-month remote internship will allow the successful candidate to contribute to research supporting a forthcoming Springer publication while developing practical skills in literature reviews, evidence synthesis, academic writing, policy research and knowledge production. The opportunity also provides exposure to a United Nations research environment and experience working within an international, multicultural setting.

With applications closing on September 18, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Macau time (GMT+8), eligible candidates should prepare their cover letter, CV and relevant research samples early and ensure that their application clearly demonstrates the research and academic capabilities required for the role.

For more global Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The C. B. Facey Foundation provides funding and support for initiatives that contribute to the development of communities through its mandated areas of Arts, Education and the Environment. The Foundation accepts grant applications during a specific annual application period, while sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted throughout the year for consideration.

For organizations, community groups, institutions and other eligible applicants working within the Foundation’s areas of interest, this presents an opportunity to seek financial support for initiatives that align with the Foundation’s mandate.

About the C. B. Facey Foundation

The C. B. Facey Foundation supports activities and initiatives within three principal areas:

  • Arts
  • Education
  • Environment

Its support is structured through different avenues, including annual grant applications, sponsorship requests and specific scholarship arrangements.

Applicants should understand that these avenues have different application procedures and timelines. In particular, the annual grant application period should not be confused with sponsorship requests, which can be submitted year-round.

C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications

The Foundation accepts grant applications annually from August 12 to October 12.

This annual application window provides an opportunity for applicants seeking financial support for eligible initiatives to submit their proposals for consideration.

Application period

The annual grant application period is:

Opening date: August 12
Deadline: October 12 each year

APPLY HERE

Applicants interested in receiving grant support should therefore prepare their proposals and supporting information before the application period opens.

Because applications are only accepted during the specified annual period, applicants should pay close attention to the dates and ensure that their submissions are made within the Foundation’s designated window.

Areas Covered by the Foundation

The Foundation’s mandate covers three major areas: Arts, Education and the Environment.

1. Arts

Organizations and initiatives working within the arts may fall within one of the Foundation’s areas of interest.

This may include activities connected to artistic and cultural development, although the information provided does not specify a complete list of eligible arts projects or the maximum amount that can be requested.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed initiative clearly demonstrates its relevance to the Foundation’s arts mandate.

2. Education

Education is another core area supported by the C. B. Facey Foundation.

Applicants seeking support for education-related initiatives should ensure that their proposals demonstrate a clear connection to educational development and fall within the Foundation’s mandated areas.

The Foundation also provides scholarships through specific educational institutions, but these scholarships operate separately from the general grant application process.

3. Environment

Environmental initiatives are also included within the Foundation’s mandate.

However, applicants should distinguish between the Foundation’s general grant applications and the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant, which is specifically intended for conservation projects.

Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant

The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Application is designed for conservation projects.

According to the information provided, the Eco-Grant application is currently closed.

This means applicants interested specifically in conservation funding should not assume that the general C. B. Facey Foundation grant application period automatically applies to the Eco-Grant.

Those interested in future conservation funding opportunities should monitor the relevant application announcements for information about when the Eco-Grant reopens.

Sponsorship Opportunities

The C. B. Facey Foundation also considers sponsorship and ticket purchase requests separately from its annual grant applications.

Unlike the annual grants, sponsorship and ticket purchase requests can be submitted year-round.

Requests must fall within the Foundation’s mandated areas of:

  • Arts
  • Education
  • Environment

Applicants or organizations seeking sponsorship should submit their requests by email to:

cbfacey@panjamaica.com

This means organizations do not necessarily have to wait until the August 12 to October 12 grant application period to request sponsorship or ticket purchase support.

However, submitting a request does not guarantee funding or sponsorship. Requests are subject to consideration by the Foundation.

How Sponsorship Requests Work

Those seeking sponsorship or requesting ticket purchases should prepare their request clearly and explain the purpose of the support being sought.

A strong request should make it easy for the Foundation to understand:

  1. Who is making the request.
  2. What activity, event or initiative is being proposed.
  3. Whether the request relates to Arts, Education or the Environment.
  4. What type of sponsorship or ticket purchase support is being requested.
  5. Why the initiative is relevant to the Foundation’s mandate.

The Foundation can then consider the request based on its own criteria and priorities.

Scholarship Opportunities

The C. B. Facey Foundation also provides scholarships, but these scholarships are not open through a general Foundation application process.

The Foundation specifically states that it grants scholarships only to:

  • Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts
  • UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture

This is an important distinction for prospective applicants.

Students interested in these scholarships must apply through the bursaries of the respective institutions.

Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts

Students interested in scholarships associated with the Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts should contact and apply through the institution’s bursary.

Applicants should not send a separate scholarship application directly to the C. B. Facey Foundation unless specifically instructed to do so.

UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture

Students interested in scholarships associated with the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture must similarly apply through the institution’s bursary.

The Foundation’s information does not indicate that these scholarships are available to students at other universities or colleges.

Important Difference Between Grants, Sponsorships and Scholarships

Applicants should understand the differences between the Foundation’s support mechanisms.

Support Type Application Period Main Areas/Recipients
General Grants August 12 – October 12 annually Arts, Education and Environment
Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant Currently closed Conservation projects
Sponsorships/Ticket Purchases Year-round Arts, Education and Environment
Scholarships Through respective institutions Edna Manley College and UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture

This distinction is important because each opportunity follows a different process.

For example, someone seeking funding for an eligible organizational project may need to use the annual grant application process, while someone seeking event sponsorship can submit a request by email throughout the year.

Similarly, a student seeking one of the Foundation’s scholarships should approach the relevant institution’s bursary rather than submitting a general scholarship application to the Foundation.

Deadline for C. B. Facey Foundation Grant Applications

The annual grant application deadline is:

October 12 each year

The application period begins on August 12.

Applicants should therefore make sure that their applications are submitted before October 12 rather than waiting until the final day.

For sponsorship and ticket purchase requests, there is no annual deadline, as requests can be emailed year-round.

The Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed.

How to Contact the C. B. Facey Foundation

Applicants and interested individuals who have questions or concerns can contact the Foundation directly.

Email: cbfacey@panjamaica.com
Telephone: 876-929-4510

The email address can be used for questions relating to grants, sponsorships, ticket purchase requests and other matters within the Foundation’s mandate.

Visit HERE to learn more about the C. B. Facey Foundation Grants 2026

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be relevant to organizations, initiatives and applicants working within the Foundation’s stated areas of interest.

Potential applicants include those involved in:

  • Arts and cultural initiatives
  • Educational initiatives
  • Environmental initiatives
  • Conservation-related projects, when the relevant Eco-Grant is open
  • Events or activities seeking sponsorship within the Foundation’s mandated areas

Students should note that the scholarship component is much more specific. According to the information provided, scholarships are limited to students applying through the bursaries of Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture.

What Applicants Should Keep in Mind

Before submitting a request, applicants should first determine which type of support best matches their needs.

If you are seeking grant funding, check whether your initiative fits within Arts, Education or the Environment and prepare your application for the August 12–October 12 annual window.

If you are seeking sponsorship or ticket purchases, you can submit your request by email at any time during the year.

If you are seeking a scholarship, confirm whether you are applying through one of the two institutions identified by the Foundation and submit your application through the appropriate bursary.

If your project is specifically focused on conservation, be aware that the Jamaica Conservation Partners Eco-Grant is currently closed and that a separate announcement may be required when applications reopen.

Conclusion

The C. B. Facey Foundation offers several forms of support for initiatives connected to Arts, Education and the Environment. Its main grant application period runs annually from August 12 to October 12, giving eligible applicants a defined window in which to seek grant funding.

Beyond the annual grant programme, the Foundation accepts sponsorship and ticket purchase requests throughout the year by email. Meanwhile, its scholarship support is specifically directed to students at Edna Manley College of the Visual and Performing Arts and the UTECH Caribbean School of Architecture, with applications handled through the respective institutions’ bursaries.

Applicants should carefully identify the appropriate funding route before submitting a request and ensure that their initiative falls within the Foundation’s stated areas of support.

Deadline for annual grant applications: October 12 each year.

Contact: cbfacey@panjamaica.com | 876-929-4510

item.content:encoded:
The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 is now accepting applications from established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers seeking dedicated time and space for research, experimentation, reflection, and creative development.

Created in 1971 by Jerome Hill, the Camargo Fellowship is the flagship residency program of the Camargo Foundation, based in Cassis, France. Over the decades, the Foundation has supported more than 1,500 individuals through its residency programs.

The 2027–2028 call offers residencies taking place in Fall 2027 and Spring 2028, giving selected fellows an opportunity to spend approximately 10 weeks in an environment designed to encourage independent work, interdisciplinary exchange, artistic creation, and research.

The Camargo Foundation describes its residency environment as a space where artists, scholars, and researchers can step away from their normal routines and dedicate focused time to developing their work. The Foundation’s current information also highlights its long-standing role in supporting artistic and intellectual exploration on the Mediterranean coast of France.

What Is the Camargo Fellowship?

The Camargo Fellowship is the Camargo Foundation’s flagship residency program, established in 1971 by Jerome Hill.

The program is designed to provide selected artists, scholars, and thinkers with the time, space, and conditions necessary for independent and rigorous work.

Rather than functioning like a conventional academic scholarship or employment opportunity, the fellowship is structured around a residency model.

During the residency, fellows can dedicate themselves to:

  • Research
  • Artistic creation
  • Experimentation
  • Writing and intellectual work
  • Reflection
  • Development of new ideas
  • Interdisciplinary exchange
  • Exploration of new approaches to their practice or research

The Foundation’s mission emphasizes supporting artistic creation and research in their various forms while encouraging exchange between different fields of knowledge.

Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Residency Period

The current call is for residencies taking place during:

  • Fall 2027
  • Spring 2028

Each residency lasts approximately 10 weeks.

This period gives fellows an extended opportunity to step away from their usual professional or academic environment and concentrate on a particular project, research question, creative practice, or intellectual investigation.

Who Is the Camargo Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship is intended for established or mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers from diverse backgrounds.

The opportunity therefore extends across multiple fields rather than focusing exclusively on one artistic discipline or academic subject.

Potential applicants may include professionals working in areas such as:

  • Visual arts
  • Literature and writing
  • Performing arts
  • Cultural research
  • Humanities
  • Social sciences
  • Other forms of scholarly or intellectual inquiry
  • Interdisciplinary artistic and research practices

The important consideration is that applicants should have an established or mid-career practice and a meaningful project or area of research that can benefit from a dedicated residency period.

What Can Fellows Use the Residency For?

The Camargo Fellowship provides a setting for research, experimentation, and reflection.

This means that the residency can be valuable for people who need concentrated time to develop work that may be difficult to pursue alongside their normal professional responsibilities.

For an artist, this could mean using the residency to develop a new body of work, explore a new creative approach, or deepen an existing artistic project.

For a scholar, it could provide time for research, writing, analysis, or development of a major intellectual project.

For a thinker or interdisciplinary practitioner, it could provide an opportunity to investigate ideas that connect different areas of knowledge and practice.

The Foundation’s broader mission is particularly focused on encouraging exchange across different fields and supporting independent, rigorous, and emancipatory work.

A Unique Opportunity for Focused Work

One of the major advantages of a residency such as the Camargo Fellowship is the opportunity to dedicate substantial time to a project without the same day-to-day pressures that can accompany normal professional or academic life.

The Foundation describes its residency environment as providing artists and scholars with an opportunity to recharge, create, and collaborate, while also offering space for personal reflection.

The 10-week residency can therefore be particularly useful for applicants who have reached a stage in their work where concentrated time and a supportive environment could help them make significant progress.

The Camargo Foundation’s International Community

The Camargo Foundation has developed an international community of artists, researchers, and thinkers throughout its history.

The Foundation’s 2025 figures, for example, indicate that it hosted 54 artists, researchers, and thinkers in residence, representing 18 countries and five continents.

This international environment is an important part of the broader residency experience.

Fellows have opportunities to work independently while also being situated within a community that brings together people working across different disciplines, cultures, and perspectives.

Why Interdisciplinary Exchange Matters

The Camargo Fellowship is not only about giving fellows a physical place to work.

The Foundation’s mission places considerable emphasis on exchange across different fields of knowledge.

Bringing artists, scholars, researchers, and thinkers together can create opportunities for people to encounter perspectives outside their usual areas of specialization.

This can encourage:

  1. New research questions.
  2. New creative approaches.
  3. Cross-disciplinary collaboration.
  4. Intellectual exchange.
  5. Broader perspectives on existing work.
  6. Development of ideas that connect different fields.

For applicants whose work sits between disciplines, this environment may be particularly valuable.

Important Change to the Camargo Fellowship Application Process

One of the most important pieces of information for prospective applicants is that the 2026 open call is expected to be the last public open call under the current system.

According to the Foundation’s announcement, beginning in July 2027, it plans to introduce a new selection process that will no longer be based on a public open call.

This makes the current application round particularly significant for artists, scholars, and thinkers who are considering applying for a Camargo residency.

The Foundation explains that the change is intended to broaden the diversity of profiles welcomed into residence and create opportunities for a wider range of:

  • Practices
  • Perspectives
  • Research themes
  • Creative approaches

The Foundation also connects this change to its broader commitment to keeping its mission relevant and renewed.

APPLY HERE

Why Applicants Should Consider Applying Now

Because of the planned change to the selection process, people who are interested in completing a Camargo residency should consider the 2027–2028 call as an important opportunity.

The current public call provides applicants with an opportunity to apply directly through the established application process.

After the new selection system begins in July 2027, prospective applicants will no longer be able to rely on the same public open-call model.

Therefore, artists, scholars, and thinkers who have been considering the Camargo Fellowship should carefully review the current eligibility requirements and submit an application if they believe their work aligns with the program.

Application Period

Applications for the 2027–2028 Camargo Fellowship opened on:

July 2, 2026

The application period runs through:

September 30, 2026

The supplied announcement also identifies October 1, 2026 as the deadline. Applicants should therefore submit their applications before the stated deadline and should verify the exact closing time displayed on the official application platform before submitting.

How to Apply for the Camargo Fellowship

Applicants interested in the 2027–2028 residency should complete the application through the Camargo Foundation’s online submission platform.

The official application platform is hosted through Submittable.

Camargo Foundation application platform

Applicants should carefully review the fellowship guidelines before beginning the application.

The Foundation’s official website provides dedicated sections for applying and reviewing residency conditions.

Review the Fellowship Guidelines Before Applying

The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Guidelines contain important information concerning the residency conditions and eligibility requirements.

Applicants should use the guidelines to confirm that:

  • They meet the eligibility requirements.
  • Their professional level is appropriate for the fellowship.
  • Their proposed project aligns with the purpose of the residency.
  • They understand the residency duration.
  • They understand the financial and practical conditions.
  • They have the required application materials.
  • They understand what is expected during the residency.

Because residency opportunities can have specific requirements that are not always captured in a short announcement, applicants should read the complete guidelines before submitting their application.

Residency Environment

The Camargo Foundation is located in Cassis, France, on the Mediterranean coast.

The Foundation’s current materials describe the location as an environment where artists and scholars can find space to reflect, create, and collaborate.

The physical setting is part of the broader residency experience, providing fellows with an environment away from the distractions of their usual routines.

The Foundation’s location, combined with its interdisciplinary community, is intended to create conditions that encourage focused work and exchange.

Webinar for Prospective Applicants

The Foundation has also provided a webinar for people interested in the fellowship.

Prospective applicants can use the webinar to better understand the program and the application process.

Applicants should consider watching the session before preparing their application, particularly if they are unfamiliar with residency programs or the Camargo Fellowship.

What Makes the Camargo Fellowship Significant?

The Camargo Fellowship has operated for more than five decades.

Since its establishment in 1971, the Camargo Foundation has supported more than 1,500 individuals through its flagship fellowship program, according to the opportunity announcement.

The Foundation’s broader recent figures also demonstrate its international reach, with residents representing multiple countries and continents.

The longevity of the program means that the fellowship is part of an established international residency tradition rather than being a newly created opportunity.

What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective fellows should think carefully about what they want to accomplish during the residency.

A strong application should clearly communicate the value of having dedicated residency time for the applicant’s work.

Applicants should consider questions such as:

  1. What project or research do I want to develop?
  2. Why is this particular period of residency important for my work?
  3. What can I realistically accomplish during 10 weeks?
  4. How does the proposed work relate to my existing practice or research?
  5. What new ideas or approaches do I want to explore?
  6. How could the Camargo environment contribute to the development of my work?
  7. What makes this stage of my career appropriate for the fellowship?

Thinking through these questions can help applicants present a clear and convincing case for their proposed residency.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028

Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 Key Details

  • Opportunity: Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028
  • Organization: Camargo Foundation
  • Established: 1971
  • Founder: Jerome Hill
  • Location: Cassis, France
  • Residency length: 10 weeks
  • Residency periods: Fall 2027 and Spring 2028
  • Target applicants: Established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers
  • Purpose: Research, experimentation, reflection, artistic creation, and intellectual work
  • Applications open: July 2, 2026
  • Application deadline: September 30, 2026 / October 1, 2026 as stated in the supplied announcement
  • Application platform: Camargo Foundation Submittable
  • Future selection change: From July 2027, selection will no longer be based on a public open call

Conclusion

The Camargo Fellowship 2027–2028 offers established and mid-career artists, scholars, and thinkers an opportunity to dedicate approximately 10 weeks to research, experimentation, reflection, and creative or intellectual development in Cassis, France.

Established in 1971 by Jerome Hill, the Camargo Fellowship has a long history of supporting individuals working across artistic, academic, and intellectual fields. The Foundation’s current international residency community demonstrates the program’s ability to bring together people from different countries, disciplines, and perspectives.

The 2027–2028 call is especially significant because the Foundation has announced that this year’s public open call will, until further notice, be the last one under the current application model. From July 2027, a new selection process will replace the public open call.

Artists, scholars, and thinkers who have been considering a Camargo residency should therefore take advantage of the current application round and carefully review the official guidelines before submitting their application.

Deadline: September 30, 2026, with the supplied announcement also stating October 1, 2026. Applicants should verify the exact closing time on the official application platform before submission.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
